text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--- Danish banks' attempts to win new customers by offering ultra cheap loans lost them close on one billion crowns in 1996 and the trend is seen continuing this year.
--- Ever-escalating illegal immigration and smuggling of refugees into Denmark by outside organisations have prompted the Danish police to demand increased vigilance from local police districts.

--- A majority in Denmark's parliament is in favour of lowering the legal blood alcohol content for car drivers from 0.8 units per thousand units of blood to 0.5 in the wake of former Conservative leader Hans Engell's drunken-driving accident which last week led to his resignation.

--- An increasing number of Danish private savers are now buying state bonds by mail order through Denmark's Mortgage Bank which last year sold 496 million Dkk worth, an increase of 24 percent compared to 1995.
--- Denmark has lost one of its main competitive advantages, its easy rules as regards hiring and dismissing staff and thus holding labour costs down, an European Union report shows.

--- Denmark's Radical Liberal Party - the Social Democrat's coalition partner in government - is pressing for the removal of children's benefits means tests on well-to-do families as part of upcoming tax reforms.
